<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api">Rebilly REST API v2.1</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

# Introduction
The Rebilly API is built on HTTP.  Our API is RESTful.  It has predictable
resource URLs.  It returns HTTP response codes to indicate errors.  It also
accepts and returns JSON in the HTTP body.  You can use your favorite
HTTP/REST library for your programming language to use Rebilly's API, or
you can use one of our SDKs (currently available in [PHP](https://github.com/Rebilly/rebilly-php)
and [Javascript](https://github.com/Rebilly/rebilly-js-sdk)).

We have other APIs that are also available.  Every action from our [app](https://app.rebilly.com)
is supported by an API which is documented and available for use so that you
may automate any workflows necessary.  This document contains the most commonly
integrated resources.

# Authentication

When you sign up for an account, you are given your first secret API key.
You can generate additional API keys, and delete API keys (as you may
need to rotate your keys in the future). You authenticate to the
Rebilly API by providing your secret key in the request header.

Rebilly offers three forms of authentication:  secret key, publishable key, JSON Web Tokens, and public signature key.
- [Secret API key](#section/Authentication/SecretApiKey): used for requests made
  from the server side. Never share these keys. Keep them guarded and secure.
- [Publishable API key](#section/Authentication/PublishableApiKey): used for 
  requests from the client side. For now can only be used to create 
  a [Payment Token](#operation/PostToken) and 
  a [File token](#operation/PostFile).
- [JWT](#section/Authentication/JWT): short lifetime tokens that can be assigned a specific expiration time.

Never share your secret keys. Keep them guarded and secure.

# Errors
Rebilly follow's the error response format proposed in [RFC 7807](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7807) also known as Problem Details for HTTP APIs.  As with our normal API responses, your client must be prepared to gracefully handle additional members of the response.

# SDKs

Rebilly offers a Javascript SDK and a PHP SDK to help interact with
the API.  However, no SDK is required to use the API.

Rebilly also offers [FramePay](https://docs.rebilly.com/docs/developer-docs/framepay/),
 a client-side iFrame-based solution to help
create payment tokens while minimizing PCI DSS compliance burdens
and maximizing the customizability. [FramePay](https://docs.rebilly.com/docs/developer-docs/framepay/)
is interacting with the [payment tokens creation operation](#operation/PostToken).

## Javascript SDK

Installation and usage instructions can be found [here](https://docs.rebilly.com/docs/developer-docs/sdks).
SDK code examples are included in these docs.

## PHP SDK
For all PHP SDK examples provided in these docs you will need to configure the `$client`.
You may do it like this:

```php
$client = new Rebilly\Client([
    'apiKey' =&gt; 'YourApiKeyHere',
    'baseUrl' =&gt; 'https://api.rebilly.com',
]);
```

# Using filter with collections
Rebilly provides collections filtering. You can use `?filter` param on collections to define which records should be shown in the response.

Here is filter format description:

- Fields and values in filter are separated with `:`: `?filter=firstName:John`.

- Sub-fields are separated with `.`: `?filter=billingAddress.country:US`.

- Multiple filters are separated with `;`: `?filter=firstName:John;lastName:Doe`. They will be joined with `AND` logic. In this example: `firstName:John` AND `lastName:Doe`.

- You can use multiple values using `,` as values separator: `?filter=firstName:John,Bob`. Multiple values specified for a field will be joined with `OR` logic. In this example: `firstName:John` OR `firstName:Bob`.

- To negate the filter use `!`: `?filter=firstName:!John`. Note that you can negate multiple values like this: `?filter=firstName:!John,!Bob`. This filter rule will exclude all Johns and Bobs from the response.

- You can use range filters like this: `?filter=amount:1..10`.

- You can use gte (greater than or equals) filter like this: `?filter=amount:1..`, or lte (less than or equals) than filter like this: `?filter=amount:..10`. This also works for datetime-based fields.

- You can create some [predefined values lists](https://user-api-docs.rebilly.com/#tag/Lists) and use them in filter: `?filter=firstName:@yourListName`. You can also exclude list values: `?filter=firstName:!@yourListName`.

- Datetime-based fields accept values formatted using RFC 3339 like this: `?filter=createdTime:2021-02-14T13:30:00Z`. 

# Expand to include embedded objects
Rebilly provides the ability to pre-load additional 
objects with a request. 

You can use `?expand` param on most requests to expand
and include embedded objects within the
`_embedded` property of the response.

The `_embedded` property contains an array of 
objects keyed by the expand parameter value(s).

You may expand multiple objects by passing them
as comma-separated to the expand value like so:

```
?expand=recentInvoice,customer
```

And in the response, you would see:

```
"_embedded": [
    "recentInvoice": {...},
    "customer": {...}
]
```
Expand may be utilitized not only on `GET` requests but also on `PATCH`, `POST`, `PUT` requests too.


# Getting started guide

Rebilly's API has over 300 operations.  That's more than you'll 
need to implement your use cases.  If you have a use 
case you would like to implement, please consult us for
feedback on the best API operations for the task.

Our getting started guide will demonstrate a basic order form use
case.  It will allow us to highlight core resources
in Rebilly that will be helpful for many other use cases
too.

Within 25 minutes, you'll have sent API requests (via our console)
to create a subscription order.

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer You can create a JSON Web Token (JWT) via our [JWT Session resource](https://user-api-docs.rebilly.com/#operation/PostSigninRequest).
Usage format: `Bearer &lt;JWT&gt;`.

* API Key (PublishableApiKey)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header. Only for the Tokens resource.
You can create a Publishable API Key via our [API Keys resource](https://user-api-docs.rebilly.com/#tag/API-Keys), by specifying the type as `publishable`.

* API Key (SecretApiKey)
    - Parameter Name: **REB-APIKEY**, in: header. When you sign up for an account, you are given your first secret API key.
To do so please [follow this link.](https://app.rebilly.com/signup)
Also you can generate additional API keys, and delete API keys (as you may
need to rotate your keys in the future). All API keys can be restricted to a
small set of permissions (restricted API keys).

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-3d-secure">3D Secure</h1>

3D Secure is a way to authenticate and protect transactions.  Typically,
it's only possible to protect the initial transaction in an order
with 3D Secure.

## Create a ThreeDSecure entry

<a id="opIdPost3DSecure"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/3dsecure \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0,
    "cavv": "string",
    "createdTime": {},
    "currency": {},
    "customerId": {},
    "eci": 0,
    "enrolled": "Y",
    "enrollmentEci": "string",
    "gatewayAccountId": {},
    "payerAuthResponseStatus": "Y",
    "paymentCardId": {},
    "signatureVerification": "Y",
    "websiteId": {},
    "xid": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /3dsecure`

Create a ThreeDSecure entry.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "cavv": "string",
  "createdTime": {},
  "currency": {},
  "customerId": {},
  "eci": 0,
  "enrolled": "Y",
  "enrollmentEci": "string",
  "gatewayAccountId": {},
  "payerAuthResponseStatus": "Y",
  "paymentCardId": {},
  "signatureVerification": "Y",
  "websiteId": {},
  "xid": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-threedsecure-entry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[ThreeDSecure](#schemathreedsecure)|true|ThreeDSecure resource.|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|Transaction amount.|
|» cavv|body|string|false|The 3D Secure entry cardholder authentication verification value.|
|» createdTime|body|object|false|The 3D Secure entry created time.|
|» currency|body|object|true|none|
|» customerId|body|object|true|Related customer ID.|
|» eci|body|integer|false|The 3D Secure entry electronic commerce indicator.|
|» enrolled|body|string|true|Is the cardholder enrolled in 3DSecure.|
|» enrollmentEci|body|string|true|The 3D Secure entry enrollment eci.|
|» gatewayAccountId|body|object|true|Related gateway account ID.|
|» payerAuthResponseStatus|body|string|false|The 3D Secure entry Auth Response Status.|
|» paymentCardId|body|object|true|Related payment card ID.|
|» signatureVerification|body|string|false|If signature was verified.|
|» websiteId|body|object|true|Related Website ID.|
|» xid|body|string|false|The 3D Secure entry transaction Id.|

|» signatureVerification|Y|
|» signatureVerification|N|

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-aml">AML</h1>

AML, also known as Anti-Money-Laundering is an endpoint that searches multiple
PEP, Sanctions, and Adverse Media lists for listed identities or media for screening
purposes. Used during some transaction processing and on Contact creation, it helps
determine whether someone is blocklisted or has political or economic sanctions against
them.


## Search PEP/Sanctions/Adverse Media lists

<a id="opIdGetAmlEntry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/aml?firstName=string&lastName=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /aml`

Search multiple PEP/Sanctions/Adverse Media lists with first and last name to find any blocklisted identities.
Performs a fuzzy search including soundex. Not all fields are guaranteed to be filled.


<h3 id="search-pepsanctionsadverse-media-lists-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|firstName|query|string|true|First name of individual to search.|
|lastName|query|string|true|Last name of individual to search.|
|dob|query|string|false|Date of birth in format YYYY-MM-DD.|
|country|query|string|false|Country of individual as an ISO Alpha-2 code.|

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-bank-accounts">Bank Accounts</h1>

Bank Accounts are a type of payment instrument used to collect
ACH (echeck) payments, similar to how a payment
card would be used to for a credit card payment.


## Retrieve a list of bank accounts

<a id="opIdGetBankAccountCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bank-accounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /bank-accounts`

Retrieve a list of Bank Accounts.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-bank-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The collection items limit.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The collection items offset.|
|q|query|string|false|The partial search of the text fields.|
|sort|query|[string]|false|The collection items sort field and order (prefix with "-" for descending sort).|
|filter|query|string|false|The collection items filter requires a special format.<br>Use "," for multiple allowed values.  Use ";" for multiple fields.<br>See the [filter guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Using-filter-with-collections) for more options and examples about this format.<br>|
|expand|query|string|false|Expand a response to get a full related object included inside of the `_embedded` path in the response.<br>It accepts a comma-separated list of objects to expand.<br>See the [expand guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Expand-to-include-embedded-objects) for more info.<br>|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

## Create a Bank Account with predefined ID

<a id="opIdPutBankAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bank-accounts/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "customFields": {
      "foo": "bar"
    },
    "customerId": {},
    "token": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /bank-accounts/{id}`

Create or update a BankAccount with predefined identifier string.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "customFields": {
    "foo": "bar"
  },
  "customerId": {},
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-bank-account-with-predefined-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[BankAccountCreateToken](#schemabankaccountcreatetoken) \| [BankAccountCreatePlain](#schemabankaccountcreateplain)|true|BankAccount resource.|

<h3 id="create-a-bank-account-with-predefined-id-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|BankAccount was updated.|[BankAccount](#schemabankaccount)|
|201|Created|BankAccount was created.|[BankAccount](#schemabankaccount)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access, invalid credentials was used.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Access forbidden.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Resource was not found.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid data was sent.|[InvalidError](#schemainvaliderror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Rate-Limit-Limit|integer||The number of allowed requests in the current period.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Remaining|integer||The number of remaining requests in the current period.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Reset|string||The date in format defined by [RFC 822](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec3.html#sec3.3.1)<br>when the current period will reset.<br>|
|201|Rate-Limit-Limit|integer||The number of allowed requests in the current period.|
|201|Rate-Limit-Remaining|integer||The number of remaining requests in the current period.|
|201|Rate-Limit-Reset|string||The date in format defined by [RFC 822](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec3.html#sec3.3.1)<br>when the current period will reset.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
SecretApiKey, JWT
</aside>

## Update a bank account's values

<a id="opIdPatchBankAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bank-accounts/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "accountType": "checking",
    "bankName": "string",
    "billingAddress": {
      "address": "36 Craven St",
      "address2": "string",
      "city": "London",
      "country": "GB",
      "emails": [
        {
          "label": "main",
          "primary": true,
          "value": "rebilly@example.com"
        }
      ],
      "firstName": "Benjamin",
      "lastName": "Franklin",
      "organization": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/ReadyToPayMethods/example/2/feature"
      },
      "phoneNumbers": [
        {
          "label": "main",
          "primary": true,
          "value": "512-710-1640"
        }
      ],
      "postalCode": "WC2N 5NF",
      "region": "London"
    },
    "customFields": {
      "foo": "bar"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /bank-accounts/{id}`

Update bank account's values except for the account number and routing. number.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accountType": "checking",
  "bankName": "string",
  "billingAddress": {
    "address": "36 Craven St",
    "address2": "string",
    "city": "London",
    "country": "GB",
    "emails": [
      {
        "label": "main",
        "primary": true,
        "value": "rebilly@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "firstName": "Benjamin",
    "lastName": "Franklin",
    "organization": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/ReadyToPayMethods/example/2/feature"
    },
    "phoneNumbers": [
      {
        "label": "main",
        "primary": true,
        "value": "512-710-1640"
      }
    ],
    "postalCode": "WC2N 5NF",

  },

    "foo": "bar"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-bank-accounts-values-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[BankAccountUpdatePlain](#schemabankaccountupdateplain)|false|Bank Account.|
|» accountType|body|string|false|Bank's account type.|
|» bankName|body|string|false|Bank's name.|
|» billingAddress|body|object|false|The billing address.|
|» » address|body|string \| null|false|The contact street address.|
|» » address2|body|string \| null|false|The contact street address (second line).|
|» » city|body|string \| null|false|The contact city.|
|» » country|body|string \| null|false|The contact country ISO Alpha-2 code.|
|» » emails|body|[ContactEmails](#schemacontactemails)|false|The list of emails.|
|» » firstName|body|string \| null|false|The contact first name.|
|» » lastName|body|string \| null|false|The contact last name.|
|» » organization|body|string \| null|false|The contact organization.|
|» » phoneNumbers|body|[ContactPhoneNumbers](#schemacontactphonenumbers)|false|The list of phone numbers.|
|» » postalCode|body|string \| null|false|The contact postal code.|
|» » region|body|string \| null|false|The contact region (state).|
|» customFields|body|[ResourceCustomFields](#schemaresourcecustomfields)|false|Custom Fields list as a map `{"custom field name": "custom field value", ...}`. The format must follow the saved format (see Custom Fields section for the formats).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» accountType|checking|
|» accountType|savings|
|» accountType|other|

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-blocklists">Blocklists</h1>

Your blocklists contains values of customerIds, email addresses,
ipAddresses, bank identification numbers, countries or payment cards that
you do NOT want to do business with. They are a good tool for managing
risk. A blocklist entry that expires after a period of time we call a
greylist.

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-coupons">Coupons</h1>

```json
      }
```

## Set a coupon's expiration time

<a id="opIdPostCouponExpiration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/coupons/string/expiration \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "expiredTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /coupons/{id}/expiration`

Set a coupon's expiry time with the specified coupon ID.
The expiredTime of a coupon must be greater than its issuedTime.
This cannot be performed on expired coupons.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiredTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

|body|body|[CouponExpiration](#schemacouponexpiration)|false|Coupon resource.|
|» expiredTime|body|string(date-time)|true|The coupon's expiry time, must be greater than the issued time. Null or empty string will immediately expire the coupon.|

`POST /customers`

Create a customer without a predefined ID.
The customer's primary address
will be used as the default address for payment
instruments, subscriptions and invoices if none
are provided.

If you wish to create the customer with a predefined
ID (which we recommend to prevent duplication), you
may use our `PUT` request described below.

Read our guide to [preventing duplicates](https://api-guides.rebilly.com/core-concepts/preventing-duplicates)
to understand more.

## Retrieve a customer

<a id="opIdGetCustomer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/customers/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /customers/{id}`

Retrieve a customer with specified identifier string.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|string|false|Expand a response to get a full related object included inside of the `_embedded` path in the response.<br>It accepts a comma-separated list of objects to expand.<br>See the [expand guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Expand-to-include-embedded-objects) for more info.<br>|
|fields|query|string|false|Limit the returned fields to the list specified, separated by comma. Note that id is always returned.|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

## Upsert a customer with predefined ID

<a id="opIdPutCustomer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/customers/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "createdTime": {},
    "customFields": {
      "foo": "bar"
    },
    "defaultPaymentInstrument": {
      "method": "payment-card",
      "paymentInstrumentId": {}
    },
    "lastPaymentTime": {},
    "paymentToken": "string",
    "primaryAddress": {
      "address": "36 Craven St",
      "address2": "string",
      "city": "London",
      "country": "GB",
      "emails": [
        {
          "label": "main",
          "primary": true,
          "value": "rebilly@example.com"
        }
      ],
      "firstName": "Benjamin",
      "lastName": "Franklin",
      "organization": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/ReadyToPayMethods/example/2/feature"
      },
      "phoneNumbers": [
        {
          "label": "main",
          "primary": true,
          "value": "512-710-1640"
        }
      ],
      "postalCode": "WC2N 5NF",
      "region": "London"
    },
    "updatedTime": {},
    "websiteId": {}
  }'
```

`PUT /customers/{id}`

Create or update (upsert) a customer with predefined identifier string.
Read our guide to [preventing duplicates](https://api-guides.rebilly.com/core-concepts/preventing-duplicates)
to understand more.

|body|body|[Customer](#schemacustomer)|true|Customer resource.|
|» createdTime|body|object|false|The customer created time.|
|» customFields|body|[ResourceCustomFields](#schemaresourcecustomfields)|false|Custom Fields list as a map `{"custom field name": "custom field value", ...}`. The format must follow the saved format (see Custom Fields section for the formats).<br>|
|» defaultPaymentInstrument|body|[PaymentInstrument](#schemapaymentinstrument)|false|none|
|» lastPaymentTime|body|object|false|The most recent time of an approved payment for the customer.|
|» paymentToken|body|string|false|A write-only payment token; if supplied, it will be converted into a<br>payment instrument and be set as the `defaultPaymentInstrument`. The<br>value of this property will override the `defaultPaymentInstrument`<br>in the case that both are supplied. The token may only be used once<br>before it is expired.<br>|

## Merge and delete a customer

<a id="opIdDeleteCustomer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/customers/string?targetCustomerId=string' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /customers/{id}`

Merge one duplicate customer to another target customer and delete the. former.

<h3 id="merge-and-delete-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|targetCustomerId|query|string|true|The customer identifier to get the data of the deleted duplicate customer.|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "http://example.com",
  "status": 400,
  "title": "string",
  "detail": "string",
  "error": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "http://example.com",
  "status": 400,
  "title": "string",

  "error": "string"
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "http://example.com",

  "detail": "string",

}
```

<h3 id="merge-and-delete-a-customer-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Customer has been merged and removed.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access, invalid credentials was used.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

|» source|body|string|false|Lead source origin (eg google, yahoo).|
|» subAffiliate|body|string|false|Lead source sub-affiliate also called a sub-id or click id in some circles (eg 123456).|

## Exchange

<a id="opIdPostAuthenticationTokenExchange"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/authentication-tokens/string/exchange \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "acl": [
      {
        "permissions": {},
        "scope": {
          "organizationId": [
            "organizationId-id-1"
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "customClaims": {
      "documents": [
        "identity-proof",
        "address-proof"
      ],
      "redirectUrl": "https://mywebsite.com"
    },
    "expiredTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "invalidate": true,
    "oneTimePassword": "123456",
    "updatedTime": {}
  }'
```

`POST /authentication-tokens/{token}/exchange`

Exchange Authentication Token for JWT.

It will also invalidate an Authentication Token by default (so it can only be exchanged once).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acl": [
    {
      "permissions": {},
      "scope": {
        "organizationId": [
          "organizationId-id-1"
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "customClaims": {
    "documents": [
      "identity-proof",
      "address-proof"
    ],
    "redirectUrl": "https://mywebsite.com"
  },
  "expiredTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "invalidate": true,
  "oneTimePassword": "123456",
  "updatedTime": {}
}
```

<h3 id="exchange-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|path|string|true|The token identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[CustomerJWT](#schemacustomerjwt)|true|none|
|» acl|body|[Acl](#schemaacl)|false|none|
|» customClaims|body|object|false|none|
|» expiredTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Session expired time. Defaults to one hour.|
|» invalidate|body|boolean|false|Whether to invalidate token after exchange or not.|
|» oneTimePassword|body|string|false|The one time password sent via an email. Should contain digits only.|
|» updatedTime|body|object|false|Session updated time.|

|» description|body|string|false|The custom field description.|
|» type|body|string|true|Type value    \| Description<br>------------- \| -------------<br>array         \| An array of strings up to 255 characters, maximum size is 1000 elements boolean       \| true or false date          \| String of format "full-date" (YYYY-MM-DD) from RFC-3339 (full-date) datetime      \| String of format "date-time" (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) from RFC-3339 (date-time) integer       \| Cardinal value of -2^31..2^31-1 number        \| Float value. It can take cardinal values also which are interpreted as float string        \| Regular string up to 255 characters monetary      \| A map of 3-letters currency code and amount, e.g. {"currency": "EUR", "amount": 25.30}<br>The type cannot be changed.<br>|

## Retrieve a dispute

<a id="opIdGetDispute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/disputes/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /disputes/{id}`

Retrieve a dispute with specified identifier string.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-dispute-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

## Create or update a Dispute with predefined ID

<a id="opIdPutDispute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/disputes/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "acquirerReferenceNumber": "string",
    "amount": 0,
    "caseId": "string",
    "createdTime": {},
    "currency": {},
    "deadlineTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "postedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "reasonCode": "1000",
    "resolvedTime": {},
    "status": "response-needed",
    "transactionId": "string",
    "type": "information-request",
    "updatedTime": {}
  }'
```

`PUT /disputes/{id}`

Create or update a Dispute with predefined identifier string.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acquirerReferenceNumber": "string",
  "amount": 0,
  "caseId": "string",
  "createdTime": {},
  "currency": {},
  "deadlineTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "postedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "reasonCode": "1000",
  "resolvedTime": {},
  "status": "response-needed",
  "transactionId": "string",
  "type": "information-request",
  "updatedTime": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-dispute-with-predefined-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[Dispute](#schemadispute)|true|Dispute resource.|
|» acquirerReferenceNumber|body|string|false|The dispute's acquirer reference number.|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The dispute amount.|
|» caseId|body|string|false|The case ID for the dispute.|
|» createdTime|body|object|false|Dispute created time.|
|» currency|body|object|true|none|
|» deadlineTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Dispute deadline time.|
|» postedTime|body|string(date-time)|true|Dispute posted time.|

|» resolvedTime|body|object|false|Dispute resolved time.|
|» status|body|string|true|The dispute's status.|
|» transactionId|body|string|true|The dispute's transaction ID.|
|» type|body|string|true|The dispute's type.|
|» updatedTime|body|object|false|Dispute updated time.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|201|Created|Dispute was created.|[Dispute](#schemadispute)|

|403|Forbidden|Access forbidden.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid data was sent.|[InvalidError](#schemainvaliderror)|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-files">Files</h1>

A File is an entity that can store a physical file and some metadata. It also provides an easy access to
its size, mime-type, user-defined tags and description thus allowing easy sorting and searching among stored
files.
There are several methods of file uploading available: multipart/form-data encoded form, RAW POST (by sending
file contents as POST body), fetching from URL (by providing the file URL via 'url' param)
Attachment is an entity that is used to link a File to one or multiple objects like Customer, Dispute, Payment,
Transaction, Order, Plan, Product, Invoice, Note. That allows to quickly find and use files related to
those specific entities.


## Retrieve a list of Attachments

<a id="opIdGetAttachmentCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/attachments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /attachments`

Retrieve a list of attachments.
You may sort by the id, name, relatedId, relatedType, fileId, createdTime, and updatedTime.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-attachments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The collection items limit.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The collection items offset.|
|filter|query|string|false|The collection items filter requires a special format.<br>Use "," for multiple allowed values.  Use ";" for multiple fields.<br>See the [filter guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Using-filter-with-collections) for more options and examples about this format.<br>|
|q|query|string|false|The partial search of the text fields.|
|expand|query|string|false|Expand a response to get a full related object included inside of the `_embedded` path in the response.<br>It accepts a comma-separated list of objects to expand.<br>See the [expand guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Expand-to-include-embedded-objects) for more info.<br>|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[File](#schemafile)]|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Pagination-Limit|integer||Items per page limit.|
|200|Pagination-Offset|integer||Pagination offset.|
|200|Pagination-Total|integer||Total items count.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Limit|integer||The number of allowed requests in the current period.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Remaining|integer||The number of remaining requests in the current period.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Reset|string||The date in format defined by [RFC 822](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec3.html#sec3.3.1)<br>when the current period will reset.<br>|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
SecretApiKey, JWT
</aside>

## Create a file

<a id="opIdPostFile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "My file description",
    "file": "R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAUEBAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAACAkQBADs=",
    "isPublic": false,
    "name": "logo.png",
    "tags": [
      "test",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /files`

Additionally, a file can be sent with:.
 - multipart/form-data POST request: in this case all property names are the same as the JSON ones (`file` is an uploaded file)
 - file body request: the file body is sent as the request body, with the appropriate `Content-Type`. No additional
 properties can be set along the request data

The following file types only are allowed:
 - jpg
 - png
 - gif
 - pdf
 - mp3


If using a Publishable Api Key, only private files can be created. The files can later on be modified or used using
 a secret API key.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "My file description",
  "file": "R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAUEBAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAACAkQBADs=",
  "isPublic": false,
  "name": "logo.png",
  "tags": [
    "test",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[FileCreateFromInline](#schemafilecreatefrominline) \| [FileCreateFromUrl](#schemafilecreatefromurl)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[FileCreateFromInline](#schemafilecreatefrominline)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[FileCreateFromUrl](#schemafilecreatefromurl)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "_links": [
    {
      "href": "string",
      "rel": "self"
    },
    {
      "href": "string",
      "rel": "self"
    },
    {
      "href": "string",
      "rel": "self"
    }
  ],
  "createdTime": {},
  "description": "string",
  "extension": "string",
  "height": 0,
  "id": {},
  "isPublic": true,
  "mime": "image/png",
  "name": "string",
  "sha1": "string",
  "size": 0,
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "updatedTime": {},
  "width": 0
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
  "title": "string",

}
```

## Update the File with predefined ID

<a id="opIdPutFile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "createdTime": {},
    "description": "string",
    "extension": "string",
    "isPublic": true,
    "name": "string",
    "tags": [
      "string"
    ],
    "updatedTime": {}
  }'
```

`PUT /files/{id}`

Update the File with predefined ID. Note that file can be uploaded with POST. only.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "createdTime": {},
  "description": "string",
  "extension": "string",
  "isPublic": true,
  "name": "string",
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "updatedTime": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-file-with-predefined-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[File](#schemafile)|true|File resource.|
|» createdTime|body|object|false|The upload date/time.|
|» description|body|string|false|The File description.|
|» extension|body|string|false|The File extension.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|false|Is the file available publicly (without authentication). If true, the permalink in the _links section contains the public URL.|

|» tags|body|[string]|false|The tags list.|
|» updatedTime|body|object|false|The latest update date/time.|

|» voidedTime|body|object|false|Invoice voided time.|
|» websiteId|body|object|true|The website ID.|
|» customerId|body|object|true|The сustomer's ID.|
|» dueReminderTime|body|object \| null|false|Time past due reminder event will be triggered.|
|» retryInstruction|body|object|false|The invoice retry instruction.|
|» » afterAttemptPolicies|body|[string]|true|The policy on the attempt finishes.|
|» » afterRetryEndPolicies|body|[string]|true|The policy on the retry ends.|
|» » attempts|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » » scheduleInstruction|body|[InvoiceRetryScheduleInstruction](#schemainvoiceretryscheduleinstruction)|true|The calculation instruction of scheduled time.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » afterAttemptPolicies|change-subscription-renewal-time|
|» » afterRetryEndPolicies|abandon-invoice|
|» » afterRetryEndPolicies|cancel-subscription|

|body|body|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|Invoice resource.|
|» abandonedTime|body|object|false|Invoice abandoned time.|
|» autopayScheduledTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Invoice autopay scheduled time.|
|» billingAddress|body|object|false|Invoice's billing address.|
|» » address|body|string \| null|false|The contact street address.|
|» » address2|body|string \| null|false|The contact street address (second line).|
|» » city|body|string \| null|false|The contact city.|
|» » country|body|string \| null|false|The contact country ISO Alpha-2 code.|
|» » emails|body|[ContactEmails](#schemacontactemails)|false|The list of emails.|

|» » lastName|body|string \| null|false|The contact last name.|
|» » organization|body|string \| null|false|The contact organization.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Invoice was updated.|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|
|201|Created|Invoice was created.|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access, invalid credentials was used.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Access forbidden.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Resource was not found.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid data was sent.|[InvalidError](#schemainvaliderror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Rate-Limit-Limit|integer||The number of allowed requests in the current period.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Remaining|integer||The number of remaining requests in the current period.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Reset|string||The date in format defined by [RFC 822](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec3.html#sec3.3.1)<br>when the current period will reset.<br>|
|201|Rate-Limit-Limit|integer||The number of allowed requests in the current period.|
|201|Rate-Limit-Remaining|integer||The number of remaining requests in the current period.|
|201|Rate-Limit-Reset|string||The date in format defined by [RFC 822](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec3.html#sec3.3.1)<br>when the current period will reset.<br>|

## Abandon an invoice

<a id="opIdPostInvoiceAbandonment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/invoices/string/abandon \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /invoices/{id}/abandon`

Abandon an invoice with specified identifier string.


<h3 id="abandon-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

## Issue an invoice

<a id="opIdPostInvoiceIssuance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/invoices/string/issue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "dueTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "issuedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /invoices/{id}/issue`

Issue an invoice with specified identifier string. It must be in `draft` status.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dueTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "issuedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="issue-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[InvoiceIssue](#schemainvoiceissue)|true|InvoiceIssue resource.|
|» dueTime|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Invoice due time. Will be set same as `issuedTime` if `null` or omitted.|
|» issuedTime|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Invoice issued time. Will be issued immediately if `null` or omitted.|

```bash
curl https://example.com/invoices/string/items \
```

```json
    "createdTime": {},
```

```bash
    "periodNumber": 0,
    "periodStartTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "productId": {},
    "quantity": 0,
    "type": "debit",
    "unitPrice": 0,
    "updatedTime": {}
  }'
```

`POST /invoices/{id}/items`

Create an invoice item.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "createdTime": {},
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[InvoiceItem](#schemainvoiceitem)|true|InvoiceItem resource.|
|» createdTime|body|object|false|Invoice item created time.|
|» description|body|string|false|Invoice item's description.|
|» periodEndTime|body|string(date-time)|false|End time.|
|» periodNumber|body|integer|false|Invoice item subscription order period number.|
|» periodStartTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Start time.|
|» productId|body|object|false|The product's ID.|
|» quantity|body|integer|false|Invoice item's quantity.|
|» type|body|string|true|Invoice item's type.|
|» unitPrice|body|number(double)|true|Invoice item's price.|
|» updatedTime|body|object|false|Invoice item updated time.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|debit|
|» type|credit|

## Recalculate an invoice

<a id="opIdPostInvoiceRecalculation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/invoices/string/recalculate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /invoices/{id}/recalculate`

Recalculate an invoice with specified identifier string.
It will recalculate shipping rates, taxes, discounts. It is useful when coupon was revoked or customer redeemed coupon after invoice was issued and you want to apply it to this invoice.


<h3 id="recalculate-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

## Reissue an invoice

<a id="opIdPostInvoiceReissuance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/invoices/string/reissue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "dueTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /invoices/{id}/reissue`

Reissue an invoice with specified identifier string. It must be issued. (status must be `unpaid` or `past-due`).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dueTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="reissue-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[InvoiceReissue](#schemainvoicereissue)|true|InvoiceReissue resource.|
|» dueTime|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Invoice due time. Will be set as current date-time if `null` or omitted.|

## Apply a transaction to an invoice

<a id="opIdPostInvoiceTransaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/invoices/string/transaction \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0,
    "transactionId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /invoices/{id}/transaction`

Apply a transaction to an invoice. The invoice must be unpaid. The transaction must have a non-zero unused amount (not fully applied to other invoices).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "transactionId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="apply-a-transaction-to-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[InvoiceTransaction](#schemainvoicetransaction)|true|InvoiceTransaction resource.|
|» amount|body|number(double)|false|Amount which needs to be applied to the invoice. Can't be more than the transaction's amount. If omitted, the lesser of the transaction's unused amount or the invoice's amount due will be used.<br>|
|» transactionId|body|string|true|Transaction to be applied to the invoice.|

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-payment-instruments">Payment Instruments</h1>

The Payment Instrument allows you to accept a variety of payment methods through a single API.


## Retrieve a list of payment instruments

<a id="opIdGetPaymentInstrumentCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment-instruments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /payment-instruments`

Retrieve a list of payment instruments.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-payment-instruments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|string|false|The collection items filter requires a special format.<br>Use "," for multiple allowed values.  Use ";" for multiple fields.<br>See the [filter guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Using-filter-with-collections) for more options and examples about this format.<br>|
|sort|query|[string]|false|The collection items sort field and order (prefix with "-" for descending sort).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The collection items limit.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The collection items offset.|
|q|query|string|false|The partial search of the text fields.|
|expand|query|string|false|Expand a response to get a full related object included inside of the `_embedded` path in the response.<br>It accepts a comma-separated list of objects to expand.<br>See the [expand guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Expand-to-include-embedded-objects) for more info.<br>|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

## Create a Payment Instrument

<a id="opIdPostPaymentInstrument"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment-instruments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "customFields": {
      "foo": "bar"
    },
    "customerId": {},
    "token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /payment-instruments`

Create a payment instrument.
If such payment card or bank account payment instrument already exists then updates it instead.

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-payment-cards">Payment Cards</h1>

Payment cards are a type of payment instrument used for credit and debit card
sales.  Rebilly securely vaults the full payment card number, and can pass it
onward securely to any gateway account to transact business.


## Retrieve a list of Payment Cards

<a id="opIdGetPaymentCardCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment-cards \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /payment-cards`

Retrieve a list of Payments Cards.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-payment-cards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The collection items limit.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The collection items offset.|
|filter|query|string|false|The collection items filter requires a special format.<br>Use "," for multiple allowed values.  Use ";" for multiple fields.<br>See the [filter guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Using-filter-with-collections) for more options and examples about this format.<br>|
|sort|query|[string]|false|The collection items sort field and order (prefix with "-" for descending sort).|
|q|query|string|false|The partial search of the text fields.|
|expand|query|string|false|Expand a response to get a full related object included inside of the `_embedded` path in the response.<br>It accepts a comma-separated list of objects to expand.<br>See the [expand guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Expand-to-include-embedded-objects) for more info.<br>|

|» » lastName|body|string \| null|false|The contact last name.|

|» » phoneNumbers|body|[ContactPhoneNumbers](#schemacontactphonenumbers)|false|The list of phone numbers.|
|» » postalCode|body|string \| null|false|The contact postal code.|
|» » region|body|string \| null|false|The contact region (state).|

|» expYear|body|integer|false|Card's expiration year.|

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-paypal-accounts">PayPal Accounts</h1>

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-payment-tokens">Payment Tokens</h1>

Payment tokens are used to reduce the scope of PCI DSS compliance.  A payment
token can be made using a different authentication scheme (refer to the public key
authentication scheme in the Authentication section), which allows you to
create a payment token directly from the browser, bypassing the need to send
sensitive cardholder info to your servers.  We recommend using this with our
Rebilly.js library, which helps you wire a form into this API resource and create
payment tokens.


## Validate a digital wallet session

<a id="opIdPostDigitalWalletValidation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/digital-wallets/validation \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "Apple Pay"
  }'
```

`POST /digital-wallets/validation`

[FramePay](https://docs.rebilly.com/docs/developer-docs/framepay/)
is the recommended way to use when validating a digital wallet session.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "Apple Pay"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-a-digital-wallet-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DigitalWalletValidation](#schemadigitalwalletvalidation)|true|Digital wallet validation request.|
|» type|body|string|true|Type of the digital wallet to validate.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|Apple Pay|

`POST /tokens`

[FramePay](https://docs.rebilly.com/docs/developer-docs/framepay/)
is the recommended way to
create a payment token because it minimizes
PCI DSS compliance.  Once a payment token
is created, it can only be used once.

A payment token expires upon first use
or within 30 minutes of the token creation
(whichever comes first).

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-plans">Plans</h1>

Plans are a template for making a subscription.  For example, you may have a plan
that has a 30-day free trial followed by a recurring charge of $19.95 per month
until canceled.  The combination of the plan and a request to make an order
will apply those instructions to create the invoices according to the plan's
schedule.


## Retrieve a list of plans

<a id="opIdGetPlanCollection"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

|» createdTime|body|object|false|Plan created time.|
|» currency|body|object|true|none|

|» pricing|body|[PlanPriceFormula](#schemaplanpriceformula)|true|none|

|» productOptions|body|object|false|Name-value pairs to specify the product options.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» recurringInterval|body|object|false|The service interval. For a one-time item, use `null`.|
|» » length|body|integer|true|The length of time.|
|» » unit|body|string|true|The unit of time.|
|» » billingTiming|body|[PlanBillingTiming](#schemaplanbillingtiming)|false|The billing timing in relation to the service period.<br>For `prepaid` plans the customer pays when the service period starts,<br>whereas, for `postpaid` plans, the customer pays when the service period ends.<br>|
|» » limit|body|integer|false|The number of invoices this subscription order will generate<br>(if 1, it will not generate any beyond the initial order creation).<br>For example, set this property to `12`, when the `periodUnit` is month and the<br>`periodDuration` is 1, for a 1 year contract billed monthly.<br>|
|» setup|body|object|false|The setup. Set `null` if no setup.|
|» » price|body|number(double)|true|The price of a setup - 0 is a valid value (for free).|
|» trial|body|object|false|The trial. Set `null` if no trial.|
|» » period|body|[PlanPeriod](#schemaplanperiod)|true|none|
|» » price|body|number(double)|true|The price of the trial. For a free trial, use `0`.|
|» updatedTime|body|object|false|Plan updated time.|
|» invoiceTimeShift|body|object|false|You can shift issue time and due time of invoices for this plan.|
|» » dueTimeShift|body|[DueTimeShiftInstruction](#schemaduetimeshiftinstruction)|false|The calculation instruction of due time.<br>This is used in conjunction with the **billing anchor** to calculate due time of invoice.<br>The chronology of due time shift is always **after**.<br>|
|» » issueTimeShift|body|[IssueTimeShiftInstruction](#schemaissuetimeshiftinstruction)|false|The calculation instruction of billing time.<br>This is used in conjunction with the **service period anchor** to calculate the time the invoice is issued.<br>|

|» » unit|week|
|» » unit|month|

|» » billingTiming|postpaid|

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-products">Products</h1>

A product describes what you sell (goods or services).
A product determines how what you sell appears on invoices and receipts.
The pricing for products is set in Plans.  One product can have many
plans.

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /products`

Create a Product.


> Body parameter

```json
  "createdTime": {},
  "customFields": {
    "foo": "bar"
  },
  "description": "string",

  "options": [
    "string"
  ],
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» unitLabel|body|string|false|The unit label, such as per `seat` or per `unit`.|
|» updatedTime|body|object|false|The product updated time.|
|» accountingCode|body|string|false|The product accounting code.|
|» taxCategoryId|body|string|false|The product's tax category identifier string.|

|q|query|string|false|The default search. It will search across resources and many fields.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

<h3 id="search-merchant-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Results keyed by resource.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access, invalid credentials was used.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Access forbidden.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="search-merchant-data-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[Search](#schemasearch)]|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Pagination-Limit|integer||Items per page limit.|
|200|Pagination-Offset|integer||Pagination offset.|
|200|Pagination-Total|integer||Total items count.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Limit|integer||The number of allowed requests in the current period.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Remaining|integer||The number of remaining requests in the current period.|
|200|Rate-Limit-Reset|string||The date in format defined by [RFC 822](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec3.html#sec3.3.1)<br>when the current period will reset.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
SecretApiKey, JWT
</aside>

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-shipping-zones">Shipping Zones</h1>

A shipping zone contains regions and countries that you ship to. Each shipping zone has its own shipping rates.


## Retrieve a list of shipping zones

<a id="opIdGetShippingZoneCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipping-zones \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /shipping-zones`

Retrieve a list of shipping zones.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-shipping-zones-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The collection items limit.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The collection items offset.|
|filter|query|string|false|The collection items filter requires a special format.<br>Use "," for multiple allowed values.  Use ";" for multiple fields.<br>See the [filter guide](https://api-reference.rebilly.com/#section/Using-filter-with-collections) for more options and examples about this format.<br>|
|sort|query|[string]|false|The collection items sort field and order (prefix with "-" for descending sort).|
|q|query|string|false|The partial search of the text fields.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|

## Create a Shipping Zone

<a id="opIdPostShippingZone"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipping-zones \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "countries": [
      "string"
    ],
    "createdTime": {},
    "name": "string",
    "rates": [
      {
        "currency": {},
        "maxOrderSubtotal": 0,
        "minOrderSubtotal": 0,
        "name": "string",
        "price": 0
      }
    ],
    "updatedTime": {}
  }'
```

`POST /shipping-zones`

Create a Shipping Zone.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "countries": [
    "string"
  ],
  "createdTime": {},
  "name": "string",
  "rates": [
    {
      "currency": {},
      "maxOrderSubtotal": 0,
      "minOrderSubtotal": 0,
      "name": "string",
      "price": 0
    }
  ],
  "updatedTime": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-shipping-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

<h1 id="rebilly-rest-api-orders">Orders</h1>

An order applies a plan's template to create invoice(s) for a customer, optionally at the appropriate scheduled intervals. A subscription order may also determine if the payment is collected automatically (with autopay set true).

## Cancel an order

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionCancellation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/subscription-cancellations \

  -d '{
    "canceledBy": "customer",
    "churnTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "createdTime": {},
    "description": "string",
    "lineItems": {},
    "prorated": false,
    "reason": "other",
    "status": "confirmed",
    "subscriptionId": {}
  }'
```

`POST /subscription-cancellations`

Cancel an order or preview the cancellation parameters before that.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "canceledBy": "customer",
  "churnTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "createdTime": {},
  "description": "string",
  "lineItems": {},
  "prorated": false,
  "reason": "other",
  "status": "confirmed",
  "subscriptionId": {}
}
```

<h3 id="cancel-an-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[SubscriptionCancellation](#schemasubscriptioncancellation)|true|Cancellation resource.|
|» canceledBy|body|string|false|Who did the cancellation.|
|» churnTime|body|string(date-time)|true|The time when the subscription will be deactivated.|
|» createdTime|body|object|false|The time of resource creation (when it is posted).|
|» description|body|string|false|Cancel reason description in free form.|
|» lineItems|body|object|false|Items to be added to the new invoice. Proration item is generated and added automatically.|
|» prorated|body|boolean|false|Defines if the customer gets a pro-rata credit for the time remaining between `churnTime` and<br>subscription's next renewal time.<br>|
|» reason|body|string|false|Cancellation reason.|
|» status|body|string|false|"draft" defines that the cancellation isn't applied on an invoice and subscription but<br>can be inspected to see the charge.<br>"confirmed" will set a subscription to be canceled when the `churnTime` is reached.<br>"completed" is a read-only status which is set by the system when the churnTime is reached.<br>The cancellation may not be changed or deleted when the status is "completed".<br>|
|» subscriptionId|body|object|true|Identifier of the canceled subscription order.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» canceledBy|merchant|
|» canceledBy|customer|
|» reason|did-not-use|
|» reason|did-not-want|
|» reason|missing-features|
|» reason|bugs-or-problems|
|» reason|do-not-remember|
|» reason|risk-warning|
|» reason|contract-expired|
|» reason|too-expensive|
|» reason|other|
|» reason|billing-failure|
|» status|draft|
|» status|confirmed|
|» status|completed|
|» status|revoked|

`PUT /subscription-cancellations/{id}`

Cancel a subscription.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "canceledBy": "customer",
  "churnTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "createdTime": {},
  "description": "string",
  "lineItems": {},
  "prorated": false,
  "reason": "other",
  "status": "confirmed",
```

<h3 id="cancel-an-order-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[SubscriptionCancellation](#schemasubscriptioncancellation)|true|Cancellation resource.|
|» canceledBy|body|string|false|Who did the cancellation.|
|» churnTime|body|string(date-time)|true|The time when the subscription will be deactivated.|
|» createdTime|body|object|false|The time of resource creation (when it is posted).|
|» description|body|string|false|Cancel reason description in free form.|
|» lineItems|body|object|false|Items to be added to the new invoice. Proration item is generated and added automatically.|
|» prorated|body|boolean|false|Defines if the customer gets a pro-rata credit for the time remaining between `churnTime` and<br>subscription's next renewal time.<br>|
|» reason|body|string|false|Cancellation reason.|
|» status|body|string|false|"draft" defines that the cancellation isn't applied on an invoice and subscription but<br>can be inspected to see the charge.<br>"confirmed" will set a subscription to be canceled when the `churnTime` is reached.<br>"completed" is a read-only status which is set by the system when the churnTime is reached.<br>The cancellation may not be changed or deleted when the status is "completed".<br>|
|» subscriptionId|body|object|true|Identifier of the canceled subscription order.|

|» reason|bugs-or-problems|
|» reason|do-not-remember|
|» reason|risk-warning|
|» reason|contract-expired|
|» reason|too-expensive|
|» reason|other|
|» reason|billing-failure|
|» status|draft|
|» status|confirmed|
|» status|completed|

`POST /subscriptions/{id}/change-items`

Change an order's items or quantities and designate when and if there should be pro-rata credits given.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "effectiveTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "items": [
    {
      "plan": {
        "createdTime": {},
        "currency": {},
        "customFields": {
          "foo": "bar"
        },
        "name": "string",
        "pricing": {
          "formula": "fixed-fee"
        },
        "productId": {},
        "productOptions": {
          "color": "red",
          "size": "xxl"
        },
        "recurringInterval": {
          "length": 0,
          "unit": "day",
          "billingTiming": "prepaid",
          "limit": 0
        },
        "setup": {
          "price": 0
        },
        "trial": {
          "period": {
            "length": 0,
            "unit": "day"
          },
          "price": 0
        },
        "updatedTime": {},
        "id": {}
      },
      "quantity": 0
    }
  ],
  "keepTrial": false,
  "preview": false,
  "prorated": true,
  "renewalPolicy": "reset"
}
```

<h3 id="change-an-orders-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[SubscriptionChange](#schemasubscriptionchange)|true|Change items request.|
|» effectiveTime|body|string(date-time)|false|The date from which the renewal time (for `reset` operations) and proration calculations are made.  If omitted, it will default to the current time.|
|» items|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » plan|body|[FlexiblePlan](#schemaflexibleplan)|true|none|
|» » quantity|body|integer|true|Number of units of the product on the given plan.|
|» keepTrial|body|boolean|false|If set to true and the subscription order has an active trial, it will use that trial further. Works with 'retain' renewalPolicy only.|
|» preview|body|boolean|false|If set to true, it will not change the subscription.  It allows for a way to preview the changes that would be made to a subscription.|
|» prorated|body|boolean|true|Whether or not to give a pro rata credit for the amount of time remaining between the `effectiveTime` and the end of the current period.<br>In addition, if the `renewalTime` is retained (by setting the `renewalPolicy` to `retain`), then a pro rata debit will occur as well,<br>for the amount between the `effectiveTime` and the `renewalTime` as a percentage of the normal period size.<br>|
|» renewalPolicy|body|string|true|The value determines whether the subscription retains its current `renewalTime` or resets it to a newly calculated `renewalTime`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» renewalPolicy|reset|
|» renewalPolicy|retain|

## Issue an interim invoice for a subscription order

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionInterimInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/subscriptions/string/interim-invoice \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "transactionId": {}
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions/{id}/interim-invoice`

Issue an interim invoice for a subscription, typically used in conjunction. with plan changes and pro rata adjustments.
This process creates an invoice, adds the subscription's line items to the invoice, and issues the invoice, and applies
payment to it if a transaction id is supplied.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "transactionId": {}
}
```

<h3 id="issue-an-interim-invoice-for-a-subscription-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[SubscriptionInvoice](#schemasubscriptioninvoice)|true|Issue an interim invoice.|
|» transactionId|body|object|false|If present, applies a payment to the invoice created.  If the payment is for the invoice total, it would be marked as paid.|

## Issue an upcoming invoice for early pay

<a id="opIdPostUpcomingInvoiceIssuance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/subscriptions/string/upcoming-invoices/string/issue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "REB-APIKEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "dueTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "issuedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions/{id}/upcoming-invoices/{invoiceId}/issue`

Issue an upcoming invoice with specified identifier string for early pay.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dueTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "issuedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="issue-an-upcoming-invoice-for-early-pay-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The resource identifier string.|
|invoiceId|path|string|true|The Upcoming Invoice ID.|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[InvoiceIssue](#schemainvoiceissue)|true|InvoiceIssue resource.|
|» dueTime|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Invoice due time. Will be set same as `issuedTime` if `null` or omitted.|
|» issuedTime|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Invoice issued time. Will be issued immediately if `null` or omitted.|

<h3 id="create-a-credit-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Organization-Id|header|[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)|false|Organization identifier in scope of which need to perform request (if not specified, the default organization will be used).|
|body|body|[PayoutRequest](#schemapayoutrequest)|true|Transaction resource.|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The transaction amount.|
|» billingAddress|body|object \| null|false|Billing address. If not supplied, we use the billing address associated with the payment instrument, and then customer.|
|» » address|body|string \| null|false|The contact street address.|
|» » address2|body|string \| null|false|The contact street address (second line).|
|» » city|body|string \| null|false|The contact city.|
|» » country|body|string \| null|false|The contact country ISO Alpha-2 code.|
|» » emails|body|[ContactEmails](#schemacontactemails)|false|The list of emails.|
|» » firstName|body|string \| null|false|The contact first name.|
|» » lastName|body|string \| null|false|The contact last name.|
|» » organization|body|string \| null|false|The contact organization.|
|» » phoneNumbers|body|[ContactPhoneNumbers](#schemacontactphonenumbers)|false|The list of phone numbers.|
|» » postalCode|body|string \| null|false|The contact postal code.|
|» » region|body|string \| null|false|The contact region (state).|
|» currency|body|object|true|none|
|» customFields|body|[ResourceCustomFields](#schemaresourcecustomfields)|false|Custom Fields list as a map `{"custom field name": "custom field value", ...}`. The format must follow the saved format (see Custom Fields section for the formats).<br>|
|» customerId|body|object|true|The customer identifier string.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|The payment description.|
|» gatewayAccountId|body|object \| null|false|Rebilly will select the appropriate payment gateway account for the transaction based on the properties of the transaction and the `gateway-account-requested` event rules configurations. If you wish to prevent Rebilly from making the gateway account selection, you may supply a gateway account id here, and it will be used instead. Only use this field if you intend to override the settings.|
|» invoiceIds|body|[[ResourceId](#schemaresourceid)]|false|The array of invoice identifiers.|
|» isMerchantInitiated|body|boolean|false|True if the transaction was initiated by the merchant.|
|» isProcessedOutside|body|boolean|false|True if transaction was processed outside Rebilly.|
|» notificationUrl|body|string(uri) \| null|false|The URL where a server-to-server notification request type `POST` with a transaction payload will be sent when the transaction's result is finalized. Do not trust the notification; follow with a `GET` request to confirm the result of the transaction. Please respond with a `2xx` HTTP status code, or we will reattempt the request again. You may use `{id}` or `{result}` as placeholders in the URL and we will replace them with the transaction's id and result accordingly.<br>|
|» paymentInstruction|body|object|false|Payment instruction. If not supplied, customer's default payment instrument will be used.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[PaymentToken](#schemapaymenttoken)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[PaymentInstrument-3](#schemapaymentinstrument-3)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[PaymentMethods](#schemapaymentmethods)|false|none|
|» paymentInstrument|body|object|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[VaultedInstrument](#schemavaultedinstrument)|false|Vaulted payment instrument.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[AlternativePaymentInstrument](#schemaalternativepaymentinstrument)|false|Alternative payment method instrument.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CashInstrument](#schemacashinstrument)|false|Cash payment instrument object.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CheckInstrument](#schemacheckinstrument)|false|Check payment instrument object.|
|» processedTime|body|string(date-time)|false|The time the transaction was processed. Can be specified only if transaction was processed outside Rebilly.|
|» redirectUrl|body|string(uri) \| null|false|The URL to redirect the end-user when an offsite transaction is completed. Defaults to the website's configured URL. You may use `{id}` or `{result}` as placeholders in the URL and we will replace them with the transaction's id and result accordingly.|
|» requestId|body|string \| null|false|The request id is **recommended**. It prevents duplicate transaction requests within a short period of time. If a duplicate request is sent with the same `requestId` it will be ignored to prevent double-billing anyone.  It must be unique within a 24-hour period.  We recommend generating a UUID v4 as its value.|
|» riskMetadata|body|[RiskMetadata](#schemariskmetadata)|false|Risk metadata used for 3DS and risk scoring.|
|» websiteId|body|object|true|The website identifier string.|

`POST /ready-to-pay`

Get available payment methods for a specific transaction or a purchase.

The payment methods order shown to a customer **SHOULD** be the same as the order in the response.

The list of available methods is generated from available [Gateway Accounts](https://user-api-docs.rebilly.com/tag/Gateway-Accounts)
intersected with the last matched [Rules Engine](https://user-api-docs.rebilly.com/tag/Rules#operation/PutEventRule)
`adjust-ready-to-pay` action on `ready-to-pay-requested` event.

If there were no actions matched for the specific request – all methods supported by the Gateway Accounts are sent.

To invert this behavior – place an all-matching rule at the very end of the `ready-to-pay-requested` event in
Rules Engine with an empty `paymentMethods` property of the `adjust-ready-to-pay` action.

`POST /transactions`

Create a transaction of type `sale` or `authorize`.
This endpoint supports two main styles of transactions:
  1. A real-time decision and response.
  2. User approval/interaction is required.

A real-time decision is very familiar.  You send a request, and
inspect the `result` of the response for `approved` or `declined`.

However, many transactions, especially those for alternative
methods, require the user to interact with a 3rd party.  You
may be able to envision PayPal, for example, the user must
give permission to complete the payment (or accept the
billing agreement).

Even payment cards may require user approval in the case of
3D secure authentication.  In the event that approval is
required, you will receive a response back and notice
that the `result` is `unknown`.  You will find that the
`status` is `waiting-approval`. And you will find in the
`_links` section of the response a link for the `approvalUrl`.

In this case you would either open the `approvalUrl` in an
iframe or in a pop (better workflow for mobile).
